title: Derive Copy for Small Types
goal: Learn when to derive Copy on custom types so passing them duplicates without calling clone.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 2 Afternoon: Copy Types

sections.text: In C++ or Java, assignment copies primitive values or references. Rust moves custom struct values by default, even if they hold only primitive numbers.

sections.caption: Without Copy, passing a Point moves ownership.

sections.text: If a struct contains only types that implement `Copy`, you can opt into copy semantics. You add `#[derive(Copy, Clone)]` above the struct definition.

sections.caption: Deriving Copy gives this struct bitwise copy semantics.

sections.text: With `Copy`, assignments duplicate the bytes in memory automatically. You never need to write `.clone()` on a `Copy` type.
Types that allocate memory, like `String` or `Vec`, cannot implement `Copy`. The compiler gives error `E0204` if you try to derive `Copy` on them.

explanation: Learn when to derive Copy on custom types so passing them duplicates without calling clone.
